notes: Complete original clobber workload is retained. Benchmark assertions cover actual public metric formatting and workload counts, with no invented throughput target. Idle monitor scheduling uses TestClock and Scope; lifecycle tests use controlled TCP peers or real brokers.

nativeTests.evidence: Transfers all 256000 original 1024-byte messages (250 MiB), retains every delivery, and compares every byte with its original source buffer without scaling the workload.

cases.upstreamTestName: disconnect - close handler is called on close

nativeTests.evidence: Stopping the broker with reconnect disabled resolves the existing closed waiter and leaves the connection closed. Both upstream variants have identical observable assertions.

Stopping the broker with reconnect disabled emits disconnect, completes the status Stream, and returns None for normal EOF closure.
Stopping the active broker selects an explicit failover peer and emits disconnect then reconnect. Public getServer confirms the selected endpoint; discovery is tested separately.
Controlled INFO advertises one new endpoint. Default policy emits an update containing one added address and grows the public server pool to two.
Sending SIGUSR2 to a real broker emits lame duck INFO; the native status consumer receives ldm.
Controlled INFO advertises one new endpoint, but ignoreClusterUpdates preserves the single configured server after a flush barrier.
Forced reconnect emits reconnect before explicit close, which terminates the active status Stream and resolves closed with None.
Eight 100 ms activity ticks against a 250 ms monitor suppress notifications; explicit cancellation releases the monitor.
TestClock advances until one missed interval is reported; callback cancellation leaves the monitor inactive.
TestClock advances until five missed intervals are reported; callback cancellation leaves the monitor inactive.
Missed count reaches three, work resets it to zero, and later time remains below the five-miss threshold without notification.
Activity every 100 ms prevents misses; the 2000 ms deadline cancels after at least six ticks, and additional time leaves count unchanged.
Changing interval, cancelAfter and maxOut replaces the scheduling generation. The old tick does not fire; the new 3000 ms cancellation deadline takes effect.
Restart replaces the scheduling generation and moves the next tick relative to restart while retaining scope ownership.
The debug/trace broker fixture starts, accepts a connection and flush, exposes the readiness log, and stops successfully.
The Effect constructor rejects an empty benchmark mode selection with a typed BenchmarkError and the exact upstream reason.
